messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - Customers using Private deployments in GCP europe-west2 are experiencing intermittent TCP resets and DNS resolution failures when reaching on‑prem gateways. Symptoms: inference RPCs failing mid-stream, TLS handshakes aborted, and SRV lookups intermittently returning outdated records. Auto-triage attached: path traces show asymmetric egress via a small subset of uplinks and high packet drop on those paths. Paging on-call.

miko_oncall: taking this. Seeing spike in connection resets ~09:11 UTC. Which customers and prefixes are we seeing?

rahul_net: oncall_net here. BGP state looks fine from our routers, but traceroutes show traffic leaving europe-west2 and returning via a different peering that blackholes MTU-fragmented packets. Suspect a peering-level MTU/PMTU problem or route used with different path MTU settings.

kara_sre: infra checks: kubeservice metrics show retries and TCP retransmits, and DNS latency for our private forwarders increased. DNS logs show an unusual number of stale SRV answers (old cluster endpoints) being served by the regional resolvers.

oliver_csm: customer impact: three Private customers affected; two have automatic hosted fallbacks and degraded but functional; one customer (health-reg) has strict customer-hosted requirement and is unable to failover. Their inference jobs are failing intermittently causing user-visible errors. I'm pinging their SE.

ops-bot: Action logged: incident.create by miko_oncall.

rahul_net: I've opened a GCP ticket and requested peering path checks and MTU profile validation. Case ref INC-GCP-99831. GCP asked for packet captures and PMTU ICMP tests.

miko_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) apply a shim that forces TCP MSS clamping on our egress NAT for affected prefixes, 2) steer traffic for impacted customer tags to europe-west1 as a fallback, 3) temporarily increase DNS TTLs to reduce SRV churn. Thoughts?

pete_platform: I can push MSS clamp at the edge quickly. Command we use: 
```
edgectl egress update --selector region=europe-west2 --tcp-mss=1200
```
I can throttle to a canary group first.

kara_sre: MSS clamp seems low-risk and addresses resets if it's MTU related. DNS TTL increase might worsen stale entries, so I'd avoid that for now. Steering to west1 will work but may violate latency SLAs. We should get customer consent for any cross-region fallback.

oliver_csm: I have the health-reg customer's SE on the line. They prefer we try MSS clamp first before fallback. They also want live timeline updates.

ops-bot: Action logged: edge.config.plan by pete_platform (tcp-mss canary).

rahul_net: GCP support responded: they see an intermediate peer performing PMTU blackhole actions when packet fragmentation occurs, and their telemetry shows intermittent ICMP unreachable messages being dropped. They are escalating to their peering infra team. ETA unknown.

miko_oncall: Pete, roll MSS clamp to 5% canary for affected prefixes and monitor resets.

pete_platform: Applying canary: 
```
edgectl egress update --selector region=europe-west2,tag=private-affected --tcp-mss=1200 --canary=5%
```

ops-bot: Action logged: edge.config.apply by pete_platform (mss clamp canary 5%).

kara_sre: Canary metrics: connection resets dropped from 18% -> 7% for canary customers. No TLS handshake failures observed in the canary group.

oliver_csm: health-reg SE reports slight improvement in canary. They want us to expand to 25%.

miko_oncall: Expand to 25% and keep monitoring. Also prepare a fallback plan to steer traffic to europe-west1 if needed. Kara, coordinate the rollback plan if MSS clamp has adverse effects.

pete_platform: Expanding to 25% now. Command used: 
```
edgectl egress update --selector region=europe-west2,tag=private-affected --tcp-mss=1200 --canary=25%
```

ops-bot: Action logged: edge.config.apply by pete_platform (mss clamp canary 25%).

rahul_net: GCP engineering says their peering infra team is performing a trace and there's a config mismatch on a peer's PMTU handling for jumbo frames. They expect a fix but no firm ETA. Suggest keeping MSS clamp in place until they fix peer config.

kara_sre: Observability note: add alert for sudden increase in TCP RSTs and for SRV/TXT DNS inconsistencies. Creating the alert now.

ops-bot: Action logged: alert.create by kara_sre (tcp-reset-alert).

miko_oncall: Handoff: I'm handing the liaison to rahul_net for GCP comms and to kara_sre for infra rollouts. I'll remain available.

ops-bot: Handoff logged: miko_oncall -> rahul_net, kara_sre (09:46 UTC).

rahul_net: Update at 10:30 UTC from GCP: their peer patched PMTU behavior and we should see improvement as caches flush. They recommend keeping MSS clamp for 30 minutes post-change, then evaluating.

kara_sre: Increasing MSS clamp to full for all affected tags (remove canary) as a precaution for 30 minutes, then we'll attempt a monitored removal. 

pete_platform: Applying to 100% for tags now. 
```
edgectl egress update --selector region=europe-west2,tag=private-affected --tcp-mss=1200 --canary=100%
```

ops-bot: Action logged: edge.config.apply by pete_platform (mss clamp 100%).

oliver_csm: Customer confirmations: health-reg and two others report resolution of mid-stream failures. One customer thanks us and requests written mitigation notes.

gcp_support_bot: GCP update: peer metric shows no ICMP blackhole events post-patch. Our resolution success for the affected prefixes is at baseline.

kara_sre: Starting a staged removal of MSS clamp: 50% -> 0% over 20 minutes, monitoring for RST increase.

pete_platform: Running staged removal: 
```
edgectl egress update --selector region=europe-west2,tag=private-affected --tcp-mss=none --policy=gradual:50%
```

ops-bot: Action logged: edge.config.update by pete_platform (mss clamp removal 50%).

miko_oncall: Observability: no regression at 50% after 10 minutes. Proceed to 0%.

pete_platform: Completed removal to 0%.

ops-bot: Action logged: edge.config.update by pete_platform (mss clamp removal complete).

rahul_net: Final network checks: BGP stable, no asymmetric path anomalies detected, PMTU probes look normal.

kara_sre: Post-incident actions: 1) Postmortem assigned to miko_oncall. 2) Create a runbook entry for MSS-clamp mitigation for PMTU blackholes. 3) Add automated detection for asymmetric path MTU symptoms (RST spike + fragment drop).

oliver_csm: I'll send a follow-up to impacted customers summarizing actions and next steps. Health-reg acknowledged service recovery and will review for residual impact.

ops-bot: Incident P1 closed: recovery confirmed at 10:56 UTC. Postmortem due in 72 hours.
